speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination, and a history of a similar swollen ankle. To understand the connection, have you noticed any fever, skin rashes, or changes in your urine color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (painful urination), young male age, and recent sexual activity is highly suggestive of this sexually associated reactive arthritis. I will now request a Urinalysis to check for sterile pyuria and inflammatory markers.
